title: Two-Level Softmax Sampling Done Right: Correcting Bias from Size Imbalance and Dispersion
claim: The standard two-stage sampler systematically over- and under-samples items by group size, and our corrections remove this bias.
layout: 3 panels side by side, shared axes, red/green over- and undersampled bands
description: Three scatter plots in a row share the same axes. The x-axis is cluster size, from about 5,000 to 45,000. The y-axis is the sampling ratio R_i^(N)(q), from about 0.4 to 4.5. Each panel has a pale red band above y=1 labeled 'oversampled' and a pale green band below labeled 'undersampled', with a gray reference line at 1. The left panel, '2LS', shows brown dots on a steep decreasing curve. Small clusters sit up near 3.5 and large clusters fall to about 0.5. The middle panel, 'S-2LS (ours)', shows blue dots clustered tightly around 1 with a slight spread. The right panel, 'SD-2LS (ours)', shows green dots lying almost exactly on the y=1 line. The eye goes first to the curved brown trend on the left, then to the flat lines in the other two panels.
caption: Sampling ratio on VK-LSVD (τ = 0.1) as a function of cluster size, averaged over queries. Standard 2LS undersamples large clusters and oversamples small ones relative to exact softmax (R(N)
abstract: Sampling from a softmax distribution is a fundamental operation in machine learning, but its linear complexity in the number of items makes exact sampling impractical at scale. Two-level softmax (2LS) sampling is a popular alternative enabling sublinear-time sampling. Assuming items are partitioned into clusters, 2LS first samples a cluster and then an item within it. In this paper, we show that, despite its advantages, 2LS introduces systematic and undesirable sampling biases, which arise from misweighting clusters by ignoring both cluster size imbalance and intra-cluster similarity dispersion. We propose two sampling methods, Size-Corrected 2LS (S-2LS) and Size- and Dispersion-Corrected 2LS (SD-2LS), which correct these biases and provide provably better softmax approximations with negligible to non-existent computational overhead. In-depth experiments on five large-scale datasets validate the improved sampling properties of our methods. We recommend their consistent use in place of standard 2LS in future work.
